messages:
Maria Chen: eval-bot flagged a regression in nightly legal-faq for rw-13b-q4-int8 — major uptick in hallucination/contradiction cases. putting samples below, tagging eng-ml :eyes:

eval-bot: nightly-evals: run=2026-11-03T02:00Z model=rw-13b-q4-int8 dataset=legal-faq baseline_fail_rate=0.7% current_fail_rate=9.4% failing_cases=134/1420 dashboard=https://internal.redwood/evals/1856004321

Maria Chen: failing sample (prompt + model output):
```
Prompt: "Does the Tenancy Act of 1984 allow landlords to evict tenants without notice for non-payment?"
rw-13b-q4-int8: "Yes, under Section 5 of the Tenancy Act of 1984, landlords can evict immediately without notice if rent is unpaid. The tenant has no right to a hearing."
Baseline (rw-13b-fp16): "No. The Tenancy Act of 1984 requires written notice and certain conditions must be met before eviction; tenants have the right to dispute in court."
```

Maria Chen: also seeing repetition loop in some answers e.g. repeated fragment "the tenant must the tenant must the tenant must" on ~12 examples. some outputs are confidently wrong (fabricated statute names/sections).

Raj Patel: thanks. recent roll included the qint packing kernel optimization (PR #3421) and a small change to per-token rounding in the quantized matmul path. feels like a quant rounding/regression.

Tim O'Leary: can someone share a repro command I can run locally quickly? prefer exact flags we use in nightly harness.

Anya Kuznetsova: repro command I used when smoke-testing yesterday: 
```
./tools/nightly_eval --model rw-13b-q4-int8 --dataset legal-faq --seed 42 --batch 8 --generate-max-tokens 256 --save-fails /tmp/fails.json --kv-align true
```
Try toggling `--kv-align false` and `--disable-dyn-quant` (internal flag) to see if behavior changes.

Tim O'Leary: running now (on my devbox with a T4 clone)

eval-bot: job spawned on runner-ml-09 by Tim O'Leary: link https://ci.redwood/jobs/78891

Tim O'Leary: quick results: matched failure rate ~8.9% locally. sample matches contradiction in earlier sample.

Raj Patel: that pretty much rules out flakiness. can we bisect to the kernel patch? last-known-good model run was on 2026-10-28 before PR #3421 landed.

Anya Kuznetsova: I ran a quick compare: rw-13b-fp16 (same weight snapshots, no q4 conversion) on same harness shows 0.9% fail. so it's definitely introduced by quant conversion/runtime.

Maria Chen: reproduction notes added to thread. I'm seeing two failure modes: (1) hallucinated/contradictory statutory references, (2) short repeated fragments. both correlate with increased token-level probability spikes in quantized path.

Raj Patel: next steps I propose: 1) bisect PRs touching quant kernels (target PR #3421), 2) run a small canary pinned to fp16 on production traffic for 24h, 3) create test that asserts no fabricated statute names (simple NER/assert match) in legal-faq eval set.

Anya Kuznetsova: temp mitigations: pin model route to rw-13b-fp16 for customer tier `enterprise` (we can do via routing-policy override), and roll back the q4 kernel on dedicated pools until we root-cause. I'll open the routing change.

Maria Chen: assigning action items: Raj -> bisect & regression test, Tim -> run expanded fails collection and upload to s3, Anya -> routing rollback + canary, I'll file the ticket and own comms with customer if needed.

ops-bot: Incident created RW-ML-842: "rw-13b-q4-int8 legal-faq hallucination/regression" assigned to eng-ml. playbook template: https://internal.redwood/incidents/RW-ML-842

Tim O'Leary: uploaded /tmp/fails.json to s3://redwood-evals/rw-13b-q4-int8/1856004321/fails.json

Raj Patel: started bisect: candidate commits between `a1c3f7d` (good) and `d9e2b4f` (bad). will post intermediate results.

Maria Chen: thanks all. can we keep updates on this thread only? I'll synthesize a short postmortem draft after we have root cause. tagging @product if rollback affects canary customers. :thumbsup:

Anya Kuznetsova: temporary routing override applied, enterprise tier pinned to fp16. monitoring dashboards set to alert on legal-faq fail_rate > 1%.

Tim O'Leary: preliminary bisect result - reverting PR #3421 locally reduces fail rate back to ~0.8%. Raj please confirm on dedicated machines. :eyes:

Raj Patel: confirming on dedicated-gpu-03: revert of PR #3421 yields fail_rate 0.85%. looks like the qint packing change introduced subtle bias. will open a follow-up PR to adjust quant rounding and add unit tests.

Maria Chen: great—closing loop for now. I'll update the incident and add the sample outputs + commands to RW-ML-842. thanks everyone. :v:
